events.headline: Colts' Tyler Warren injures groin in Wednesday joint practice with Falcons
events.detail: Warren went down clutching his groin while running a route in 11-on-11 drills during Wednesday's (Aug. 19) joint practice against Atlanta and did not return to full work, later seen on the sideline without his helmet with the area wrapped. Coach Shane Steichen had no severity update but said the team would be cautious. Warren caught 76 passes as a rookie in 2025, making him Indianapolis' most-targeted pass catcher.
events.so_what: This format's punt-TE doctrine treats a locked-in target hog like Warren as a real value outlier worth paying up for, so any missed camp time on a first-round-caliber pass-catching tight end is a legitimate price risk three days before this league's 2026-08-23 draft. No structural diagnosis yet; watch for a practice-return date or an MRI result rather than pricing in a discount off a soft-tissue scare alone.

events.headline: Saints' Alvin Kamara suffers MCL sprain, out at least a month; Etienne set for workhorse role; IR stint possible
events.detail: Kamara sustained an MCL sprain during Tuesday's (Aug. 18) joint-practice scrimmage against the Cowboys. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports he'll miss at least a month, a timeline that puts the Sept. 7 regular-season opener and likely Week 2 in jeopardy. Travis Etienne, signed this offseason as the Saints' presumptive lead back for the post-Kamara transition, is now positioned to handle a workhorse-level early-down and passing-down role in his absence. Assuming the sprain follows the pattern of Kamara's past knee injuries, the recovery could stretch to four-to-six weeks; the Saints' Week 2 game at Baltimore sits right at the early end of that window (32 days out), and the team is expected to let his recovery play out before setting a firm return target, leaving a season-opening IR stint on the table.
events.so_what: This format's bell-cow-friendly half-PPR/2-FLEX math rewards exactly this kind of touch consolidation — Etienne jumps from committee-adjacent to a clean top-20 overall price for as long as Kamara is out, while Kamara himself is a tough hold on a 5-man bench this close to the 2026-08-23 draft: he won't play Week 1, may not be ready for Week 2 either, and may not be healthy enough to roster over a streamer until his practice status clears — an IR stash is a real possibility once the Saints finalize their 53. Draft Etienne like the workhorse he's about to become, not the committee back his ADP still reflects.

events.headline: Texans' Jayden Higgins tears ACL in joint practice, out for the season
events.detail: Higgins, a 2025 second-round pick coming off 525 yards and six touchdowns as a rookie, tore his ACL Tuesday (Aug. 18) during a joint practice against the Raiders, falling awkwardly on a red-zone route in 11-on-11 drills. He's done for 2026. Xavier Hutchinson (35 catches, 428 yards, 3 TDs in 2025) is the presumed direct beneficiary of the vacated WR2 targets, though Tank Dell (still working back from a serious Dec. 2024 knee injury) and Jaylin Noel (broken finger, hamstring tightness this camp) are both fighting their own availability questions behind Nico Collins.
events.so_what: A clean WR2 vacancy behind a locked WR1 is usually a real price bump in this format's normal-depth WR math, but here it's murkier than a simple 'next man up' story — Hutchinson gets first crack, yet Dell's and Noel's own camp injuries mean none of the three should be priced as a clean, healthy target earner yet. Collins himself is unaffected at WR1 and could see a marginal red-zone bump. Worth a speculative-price watch on Hutchinson through the last few days before this league's 2026-08-23 draft, not a locked WR3 grade.

events.headline: McCaffrey still hasn't practiced through Aug. 19 joint session; Shanahan continues to dismiss hold-in read
events.detail: McCaffrey sat out Tuesday's (Aug. 18) and Wednesday's (Aug. 19) joint practices against the Chargers, extending his absence to more than a week and a half since first sitting Aug. 8-10 with what the team calls tightness. Shanahan has repeatedly and directly denied hold-in speculation tied to McCaffrey's non-guaranteed $12.5M 2026 salary, reiterating the team is being cautious with a back who logged a league-high 413 touches last season, and continues to voice confidence McCaffrey will be ready for the Sept. 10 opener in Australia.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 15/16/17/18 items — a second straight joint-practice DNP pushes the absence past ten days with still no actual practice-return date, which starts to matter for this league's 2026-08-23 draft even with the hold-in theory repeatedly denied on the record. Still this format's clearest bell-cow RB1 on talent and touches, but downgrade from a fully clean grade to 'watch for an actual return rep' until he's back on the field.

events.headline: Nacua's civil case gets a firm March 2028 trial date; NFL suspension decision still pending independently
events.detail: A Los Angeles County judge set a 'firm trial date' of March 27, 2028 (about six days, with a final status conference set for March 14, 2028) for the civil suit accusing Nacua of biting a woman on the shoulder at a New Year's Eve party; the judge said there would be no continuances without good cause. The 2028 date means the NFL's personal-conduct-policy review, which does not have to wait for the civil case to resolve, remains the only clock that actually matters for a 2026 suspension. Nacua was passed over in the league's Aug. 14 suspension batch (see the earlier version of this item), and reporting since has continued to frame a Week 1 suspension as possible but not the expected outcome.
events.so_what: Updates the prior version of this item — pinning the civil trial nearly 19 months out confirms this format's near-term question (is Nacua active for this league's 2026-08-23 draft and Week 1) rides entirely on the NFL's own independent process, not the court date. Treat him as the safer-than-worst-case top-5 WR price the earlier reporting described, with the suspension risk still unresolved as a small in-season discount rather than a season-opening one.

events.headline: Giants officially sign Najee Harris to one-year deal, release JuJu Smith-Schuster
events.detail: New York made it official Tuesday (Aug. 18), signing free-agent RB Najee Harris to a one-year contract after his Monday workout impressed coach John Harbaugh, and releasing WR JuJu Smith-Schuster in a corresponding move (also captured in the separate Aug. 18 JuJu item). Harris rushed for 1,000+ yards in each of his four seasons in Pittsburgh before tearing his Achilles three games into a 2025 stint with the Chargers; he's now working back into a Giants backfield that already lists Skattebo and Tracy as co-starters on the Aug. 12 depth chart, plus Devin Singletary.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 18 item — a completed signing, not just a visit, confirms the bearish read for both Skattebo and Tracy in this format's volume-friendly scoring: a real veteran addition, even on a prove-it deal and coming off a major injury, further muddies an already-even co-starter split. Don't lock either incumbent into a set draft-round price until real preseason snaps show who's actually getting the Week 1 bulk of touches, now a three-way question at minimum ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Giants release JuJu Smith-Schuster from crowded, injury-thinned WR room
events.detail: New York released Smith-Schuster during camp Tuesday (Aug. 18). He'd been limited by a knee injury through much of camp, sat out the preseason opener, and was buried behind Nabers, Wan'Dale Robinson and others on the depth chart, with rookies getting extended run in his place. The move comes the same week the Giants hosted (and then signed, see the separate Aug. 18 Najee Harris item) free-agent RB Najee Harris and continued thinning out a receiver corps still centered on Nabers' recovery.
events.so_what: Roster-crunch confirmation only — Smith-Schuster was never a rosterable name in this format's shallow-bench build (5 bench spots, no room for WR4 depth), so this doesn't move any HBGBs draft price directly. Filed as landscape context on the Giants' post-JuJu WR corps (Wan'Dale Robinson the clear No. 2 behind Nabers) rather than a standalone signal.

events.headline: Jaguars' LeQuint Allen suffers soft-tissue injury, out for rest of camp; Tuten/Rodriguez picture largely unchanged
events.detail: Allen, the passing-down specialist in Jacksonville's backfield-by-committee (valued for pass-protection more than touches — 33 carries for 148 yards in 2025), suffered a soft-tissue injury Monday (Aug. 17) and will miss the rest of training camp; his regular-season status is uncertain. OC Grant Udinski says the backfield has "kind of been by committee in the run game... [and] the pass game" all camp, with Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. still separated only by an "OR" atop the unofficial depth chart. Beat analysis frames the direct ripple to Tuten/Rodriguez as limited since neither shares Allen's specific pass-blocking role, though Tuten — the better pure pass-catcher of the two — could see a modest bump in passing-down work.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 15 item — losing the room's clearest role specialist doesn't resolve the Tuten/Rodriguez timeshare this format most needs settled, since 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, not a three-way split. Both stay priced as speculative RB4/handcuffs rather than clean starters; watch the next preseason game for real separation before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Bears' Kyle Monangai hyperextends knee in practice, out multiple weeks
events.detail: Monangai, projected as Chicago's RB2 behind D'Andre Swift, hyperextended his right knee Sunday (Aug. 16) after being tackled from behind during a non-padded 11-on-11 period — his second camp injury after an earlier soft-tissue issue. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the MRI outcome is considered positive (no structural damage), but he's still projected to miss multiple weeks, with about four weeks left before Chicago's Week 1 opener.
events.so_what: This format's 5-man bench rewards a clean handcuff assignment — Roschon Johnson is the practical beneficiary of Monangai's lost camp reps for the RB3 job behind Swift, while Monangai himself slides from a speculative complementary-back price to a wait-and-see grade until he's back running. Swift's bell-cow workload projection is unaffected either way, so this is a depth-chart note rather than a top-of-roster shift ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: 49ers' Mike Evans exits joint practice again with tightness, three days after returning from quad strain
events.detail: Evans missed about a week of practice with a quad strain (first reported Aug. 11) before returning Aug. 15. He then left Tuesday's (Aug. 18) joint practice against the Chargers early, iced at first on his foot/ankle and then his quad, with Shanahan calling it precautionary: 'They just said he has some tightness, so we were just being smart, taking him out... I don't think it's anything worse.'
events.so_what: Directly informs the Aug. 13 Pearsall item's target-share math — Evans is still the presumed top target in Kyle Shanahan's offense ahead of Deebo Samuel and Jauan Jennings, but a second exit inside a week, at 33, is a real durability flag for a clean WR1 price rather than a one-off. Watch for him back to full, unlimited practice reps as the next real signal before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Jets' Breece Hall: MRI confirms groin strain, Jets 'dodge worst-case scenario'
events.detail: Hall left Monday's (Aug. 17) practice early with a groin strain after going down untouched following a catch on rain-slicked grass. An MRI Tuesday (Aug. 18) confirmed the shared diagnosis of a strain rather than something more severe, and beat coverage frames it as sidelining him roughly two-to-three weeks and out for the rest of the preseason, with an optimistic outlook for the Week 1 opener. Coach Aaron Glenn had already downplayed it same-day ('I don't think it was a big deal'), and the imaging result backs that read.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 17 item — the MRI confirming a straightforward strain (not a tear) keeps Hall priced as this format's clean bell-cow RB1/2 off a 1,065-yard, 36-catch 2025, though missing the rest of the preseason is a real accumulation of lost camp reps a week before this league's 2026-08-23 draft. Recheck for an actual return-to-practice date rather than pricing him at a full discount or a full clean grade off imaging alone.

events.headline: Panthers sign veteran TE Darren Waller, muddying Tremble/Sanders hierarchy
events.detail: Carolina agreed to a one-year deal with Waller (33) on Monday (Aug. 17). Waller is a 10-year veteran and Pro Bowler who led all tight ends with 107 catches in 2020 and caught six touchdowns in nine games for Miami last season. He joins a Panthers TE room that had been sorting out a hierarchy between incumbent Tommy Tremble (had the early inside track per the unofficial depth chart) and 2024 draftee Ja'Tavion Sanders, who's also drawn some first-team TE1 mentions of his own.
events.so_what: This format's punt-TE doctrine (league-profile.md) treats a settled TE1 as pure late-round or waiver filler, so a fresh veteran target-earner walking into an already-unsettled room is a real complication — neither Tremble nor Sanders should be priced as a locked passing-game piece until practice reps show who actually wins the job, and Waller himself is speculative on a prove-it deal at his age. Watch camp snaps over the next week before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Nabers takes first full-speed live team reps since ACL tear
events.detail: Monday (Aug. 17), Nabers ran four routes in 11-on-11 drills and caught passes on all three of his 7-on-7 targets while wearing the red no-contact jersey usually reserved for quarterbacks — his first live team work since tearing his ACL in Week 4 of last season. "It was good, felt good... getting some team reps, getting out there, catching the football," he said. Coach John Harbaugh called it an important step but stopped short of a Week 1 guarantee: "I don't think he's full speed yet or anything... you can hope." 27 days remain before the Sept. 13 opener at Dallas.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 15 item — actual full-speed team reps (even in a no-contact jersey) is real forward progress beyond the 'not suited up for the preseason opener' grade, trimming (not erasing) the Week 1-availability discount on Nabers' WR1 price in this format's half-PPR target-hog math. Still hold at a modest discount to a clean price until he's cleared for contact; direct stash relevance for bwalsh89, this league's Nabers/Dart owner from 2025.

events.headline: DeVonta Smith returns to practice, limited to individual drills
events.detail: Smith was back on the field Monday (Aug. 17) after missing the prior week-plus with the hamstring injury first reported Aug. 4 — a real practice sighting following the run of DNPs (up to seven straight per the Aug. 13 item). He was limited to individual drills rather than full team work as the Eagles ramp toward joint practices with the Patriots this week.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 13 item — an actual on-field return (even limited to individual work) is the concrete progress signal that item was waiting on, keeping Smith's locked-in WR1 price on track in this format's half-PPR target-hog scoring. Recheck for full team drills as the next checkpoint before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Cardinals rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) unlikely to play again in preseason, Week 1 murky
events.detail: Love, the No. 3 overall pick, suffered an ankle injury (reported by multiple outlets as a high-ankle sprain, though Arizona hasn't confirmed that label) on a 7-yard catch late in the second quarter of the Aug. 13 preseason win over the Raiders. He's expected to miss the rest of the preseason, and the team hopes he's ready for the Sept. 13 opener against the Chargers, but his status remains uncertain. Before the injury, Love had been taking first-team snaps on Arizona's first three offensive drives and out-targeting free-agent addition Tyler Allgeier 4-to-1 in one practice — a real role expansion beyond his early camp reps as the No. 2 back.
events.so_what: This format's bell-cow math wants clean separation from a crowded backfield, and Love had just started showing it before the injury hit, so the missed camp reps are a genuine markdown on a rookie-price-tag RB right before this league's 2026-08-23 draft. Allgeier and 10th-year veteran James Conner (himself still without a full-practice timetable per Aug. 15 reporting) both stand to pick up the vacated reps in the meantime, keeping Arizona's whole backfield a muddled committee grade until Love is back running at speed.

events.headline: Kittle 'very confident' he won't open season on PUP, targets practice return 'sooner than later'
events.detail: Still on PUP as of Aug. 16, Kittle was asked directly how confident he is about avoiding a Week 1 PUP start and said "Very confident," adding his return to practice would come "sooner than later." He says he's hitting recovery benchmarks, including GPS running-speed data, and called the next two weeks "everything" for determining whether he's ready for the Week 1 opener against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 15 item — a direct, on-record 'very confident' plus a 'sooner than later' timeline is a stronger positive signal than the general optimism captured earlier, but he still hasn't logged a practice rep as of this report. This format's punt-TE doctrine (league-profile.md §4) still treats a clean Kittle Week 1 as a real elite-TE outcome worth planning for, not banking on; watch for the actual PUP-list removal as the hard confirmation before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Panthers' Jonathon Brooks gets real preseason run in first live action since 2024 ACL tear
events.detail: With Hubbard held out (hamstring — coach Dave Canales called it "a legit hamstring" and week-to-week after an MRI, first reported Aug. 13), Brooks started and played 4 of the Panthers' 9 first-team offensive snaps in Saturday's (Aug. 15) preseason opener at Buffalo — 3 carries for 5 yards and 1 catch for 9 yards — his first game action since Week 14 of his rookie 2024 season. Panthers.com reports the staff intends to keep featuring him as a pass-catcher through the preseason. The team remains confident Hubbard will be ready for the regular-season opener.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 13 item — actual first-team preseason snaps (not just practice buzz) is a stronger signal of a real complementary role forming behind Hubbard, and the pass-catching usage plan makes Brooks more than a pure handcuff in this format's 2-FLEX math if Hubbard's hamstring lingers. Hubbard remains the safer lead-back price given the team's Week 1 confidence, but Brooks is worth a FLEX-speculative price ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: RJ Harvey gets first-team touches but modest numbers in Broncos preseason debut
events.detail: Harvey took all the first-team carries and ran more routes than third-down back J.K. Dobbins in Denver's preseason opener (Aug. 15), but the return was thin: 7 carries for 25 yards (two runs of 18 combined, the other five going for six total) and 1 catch for 4 yards on 2 targets. Sean Payton said afterward Harvey could have been more patient on one run and that the staff will get him more work between the tackles, calling him 'an extremely instinctive runner.'
events.so_what: The touch distribution (all 1s-work over Dobbins, who remains limited with a soft-tissue issue per the Aug. 14 item) is the clean signal for a locked-in early-down role in this format's bell-cow-friendly scoring, even though the per-carry numbers themselves don't move the needle — hold Harvey at his current early-round RB price and treat this as role confirmation, not a production data point, ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Burden doing light on-field work, sprinting routes, as groin injury trends toward a Week 1 return
events.detail: Burden's Saturday (Aug. 8) groin injury will keep him out through Chicago's preseason slate, but he was seen doing light work Saturday (Aug. 15), including sprints from the 40 to the end zone, per Adam Schefter — the first real on-field progress reported since the injury. Coach Ben Johnson still expects him back for the Sept. 13 regular-season opener at Carolina. Burden is stepping into the WR2 role opposite Rome Odunze now that Chicago traded DJ Moore to Buffalo, with Johnson comparing his ceiling to Amon-Ra St. Brown's.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 10 item — sprinting work a week after the injury is the clearest positive signal yet for a clean Week 1 return, keeping Burden's expanding target share (Moore fully gone from the room) priced as a breakout-candidate WR2/3 in this format's half-PPR/normal-depth WR math. Recheck once he's back to full team drills or a preseason snap count.

events.headline: Saints rookie WR Jordyn Tyson suffers hamstring injury in joint practice, could linger to Week 1
events.detail: Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick who fell out of top-5 consideration partly due to hamstring issues at Arizona State, injured his right hamstring Thursday (Aug. 13) in joint practice against Jacksonville after his foot slipped and he was pushed from behind following a catch. Coach Kellen Moore declined to give a timeline Thursday (Aug. 14): 'I don't have a doctor in front of my name, so I'm not going to jump to put together a timeline on it,' but said it could extend into Week 1. He was already slated to sit out that Saturday's preseason game.
events.so_what: A first-round rookie WR with a recurring hamstring history losing camp reps right before this league's 2026-08-23 draft is a real discount on his rookie-WR price in this format's normal-depth WR math — treat him as a wait-and-see Week 1 role bet rather than a locked-in target earner, and watch for the actual return-to-practice date as the next checkpoint.

events.headline: MarShawn Lloyd starts and takes every first-drive snap in Packers' preseason opener as Jacobs sits with groin injury and live suspension risk
events.detail: With Jacobs out (groin, first reported Aug. 6), Lloyd started Green Bay's preseason opener Thursday (Aug. 13) and took every snap on the first drive, working on early downs, in the passing game and in pass protection. Separately, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported this week (Aug. 11-14) that Jacobs' personal-conduct-policy investigation (stemming from a May 2026 domestic-disturbance call with no charges filed) remains open with the league still weighing discipline, and a suspension is a real possibility before Week 1; the policy sets a six-game floor for a first domestic-violence violation. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Friday (Aug. 14) that Jacobs could return to practice as soon as next week, likely coming back late in the week if he does, and continues to call the groin injury not serious.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11/13 items — LaFleur's 'back next week' framing caps the groin issue itself as a short-term markdown, but the genuinely live suspension threat with no resolution timeline is still the bigger risk to Jacobs' draft price: a multi-week absence to open the season would hand Lloyd real starting-caliber volume in this format's bell-cow-friendly scoring. Worth actually rostering Lloyd as insurance given the shallow 5-man bench, and shading Jacobs down from a clean early-round RB price until the league rules, ideally before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Dobbins limited to individual work as Broncos beat Falcons 27-7 in preseason opener; Coleman gets extensive run
events.detail: Dobbins remained limited to individual drills for Friday's (Aug. 14) preseason opener at Atlanta and did not play, still working back from the soft-tissue issue first reported Aug. 10. With Dobbins out, rookie Jonah Coleman got an extensive workload in the 27-7 win, continuing the camp buzz around his role.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 10 item — a full missed preseason game, not just a practice absence, is a real accumulation of lost reps for Dobbins against a rookie who keeps taking advantage of every opportunity handed to him. Still hold Dobbins as the lean for Denver's early-down role, but Coleman's price now needs to reflect genuine handcuff-plus-touchdown-usurper upside rather than a pure camp-buzz speculative flier; recheck once Dobbins is back to full team drills.

events.headline: 49ers' Ricky Pearsall undergoes season-ending PCL surgery
events.detail: Pearsall announced on Instagram Thursday (Aug. 13) that he had surgery to repair the PCL in his right knee, ending his 2026 season before it started. The knee had been persistently swollen through camp after he first injured it in Week 4 of 2025; his targeted recovery window is roughly nine months, putting a return around mid-May 2027 OTAs. He's played just 20 of a possible 51 regular-season games across his first three NFL seasons.
events.so_what: San Francisco's WR2 job behind Mike Evans (Aug 11/18 items) is now fully vacant before the draft, not just contested — Deebo Samuel is the likeliest full-time beneficiary of the vacated snaps in Kyle Shanahan's run-funnel offense, with Jauan Jennings the clear No. 3. In half-PPR/2-FLEX, this removes a name some boards still carried as a discount buy and nudges Samuel's price up a notch in the McCaffrey/Kittle/Evans-led target pecking order.

events.headline: Titans' Pollard-Spears split looks genuinely even in preseason opener under new OC Brian Daboll
events.detail: In Thursday's (Aug. 13) preseason opener, Pollard played 57% of snaps (50% of designed rushes, 33% route participation, 2 catches for 11 yards, 35 rush yards) against Spears' 43% of snaps (38% of rush attempts, 50% route participation, a rushing TD on 3 carries for 2 yards). The beat read: "the coaching staff has told us multiple times that they view Pollard and Spears interchangeably, which matches Week 1 of the preseason." Daboll was hired as Tennessee's OC this offseason under new HC Robert Saleh.
events.so_what: This format's top RB tier wants one back consolidating touches, not a genuine timeshare — an actual even preseason split under a new play-caller is a real markdown on Pollard's price relative to a clean lead-back valuation, and it bumps Spears from pure handcuff to a real FLEX-relevant piece if the split holds. Both currently project more as touchdown-or-bust RB3s than clean starters; recheck preseason Week 2 usage.

events.headline: Holani tops Seahawks' preseason RB depth chart over rookie Price with Charbonnet still on PUP
events.detail: Seattle's preseason depth chart (Aug. 12) lists Holani as the starting running back with first-round rookie Jadarian Price backing him up, while Charbonnet remains sidelined on the PUP list recovering from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 season, with ESPN reporting he may not return until late in 2026. Holani and Price have alternated first-team reps through camp, with free-agent addition Emanuel Wilson working mostly with the second unit. New OC Brian Fleury (replacing Klint Kubiak) is calling the offense.
events.so_what: Another crowded backfield is this format's worst RB outcome — 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, and Seattle now has three-plus bodies (Holani, Price, Wilson, and eventually Charbonnet) mixing in with no clear hierarchy. Holani's depth-chart nod plus early receiving-down usage makes him the safer near-term price, Price the higher-variance rookie speculative add; neither should be priced as a clean starter until preseason snap counts show real separation, and Charbonnet's return timeline (real question mark past Week 1) caps the whole room's value ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.
